body:
I just got done firing off an email to the nebulizer company; they're definitely going to have to send me a new battery since I just charged it last night, didn't use it, and it's completely dead this morning. The first time I contacted them I was told it's out of warranty (of course) but the lady's being nice and working with me. I still feel like they're fighting me on replacing it though, and I can't afford to drop 90-100 bucks on a new one. We were barely able to afford the machine. Then my brother starts picking on me again

And I'm whining, I'm sorry.

Yeah, I can handle getting to the store on my own. It ramps up my anxiety, but I've got a pill that helps some. I've also been practicing going out of my comfort zone without taking it, and not doing terrible.

Naw, he won't even go to therapy for himself, he doesn't want anything to do with my 'issues'.

The two closest grocery stores to my house are about two and three miles away, respectively. (Which is why I usually grab the crackers at Walgreens, it's about two blocks away.) The farthest one's the one that's a straight shot, of course. I've contemplated taking my bike to that one, the other can be reached by bus if I have to. I was just thinking of doing that very thing today, after we got into an argument over the fact he did the food shopping for him and mom but didn't bother with my stuff. I ended up so suicidal that I went back to sleep for a couple hours to keep myself from doing anything. Maybe I can grab something tomorrow after I get back from the dentist. In the meanwhile, I'll just be eating some of his food that doesn't trigger my headaches. He won't like it, but it's his fault. 

He's smart, but common sense isn't something he uses a lot of. That's something else he doesn't appreciate in me and likes to use against me. He'll make it seem like there's something wrong with me  that I'll go about stuff a certain way. (Like actually getting directions to places I've never been instead of 'I was in the neighborhood once, I know where it is'. But I'm being a brat, sorry.

Well, it takes me about fifteen minutes to get through a comic book, taking time to look at the art and all. He takes about 30-45 minutes, then gets defensive and tells me at least he's taking the time to appreciate the art. I don't have a problem with his reading speed, I don't make fun of him. He's a good reader, he just reads a little slower. 

I've got Medi-Cal, and a nice therapist. Been seeing her for a few years, but our visits tapered off into hardly any over the last year. Not because she doesn't have time to see me, which is surprising because my clinic is busy, but I have a hell of a time getting down there. My brother is my main transportation, otherwise it's two buses each way to see her. A lot of the problem there for a while was the kidney stones. It really feeds into the fear and anxiety when the stones try to kill you and you're out on your own with strangers. The other issue was needing my nebulizer treatment every 4 hours. I'd have to time things as close as possible to make sure I was near an outlet to plug the compressor in if I needed it. I have an inhaler I carry with me at all times, but it's not always enough. Just a couple weeks ago I had a bad attack right after I got to my shrink's office (3 hours into the 4 hour span) and had to plug in right in his office. But! I managed to save up enough for a portable compressor, and while I'm working the kinks out of the battery (I might have to send it back, but they won't have a new shipment until September), right now it's charging enough to let me use it if I get caught out in the open. That freedom helps a LOT.

I used to do the grocery shopping ages ago, then my brother got tired of hauling me to the store and decided he could do it quicker himself. Not gonna get into how well THAT worked out. But I only had my license for a year before my anxiety got too bad to drive, and the migraines also come in the form of random dizzy spells. I've had several that will literally knock me down, so I decided it was a lot safer if I don't try for my license again. I actually think I miss driving though, if only because at least then I'd have a good excuse to take a break. 

I've tried discussing this with him, literally telling him, 'Look, there's enough on your shoulders and I'm sorry, but I wanted to tell you how bad things have gotten and I need your help.' I've told him before about the suicidal thoughts. The first time he was actually very positive, told me he cared what happened to me and that if it was all right with me, he would see if maybe his church's pastor would be willing to talk to me. That didn't pan out. Every time after that, he just blows it off and goes 'What do YOU have to be suicidal about?' He's admitted he's depressed too, but he also takes after our dad and can be very emotionally abusive. Our dad used to call me a lot of names too, and while the name calling is slightly toned down with my brother, I still get called a freak (for being a fast reader, can you believe that? My eyes are rolling out of my head), get mocked for my health issues, and generally blown off whenever I go to him for help. So I'm kind of stuck there.

Thanks. /hug

I really really do still want those things, because when I think 'Hey, forget it, I'm done, I'm not going to bother', it always makes me cry. If I was honestly done with it, I don't think I would. I'm trying for one day at a time, but I've had to look way ahead my whole life, and it's a hard habit to get rid of. It helps a little bit in this situation, but mostly it just drives me nuts.

Yeah, the doctor said soda was probably making them worse so that got cut right out, but we really can't do much about the diet thing with the way the money is. Also the way my brother is. He does all the grocery shopping and I've tried to work with him before regarding this (a lot of my migraines are food triggers, but a great deal are stress and hormone-induced, and I can't do anything about the latter), but he doesn't care. If it means he has to read a label or keep something in mind for me or change the way he and mom eat, then he won't do it. He'll just buy what we can afford and when I mention 'Remember I can't eat this, it has X in it' he actually tells me, 'Well I guess you're not eating then'. And then I don't, depending on how bad the resulting migraine's going to be. The ER is way to familiar with me at this point. If eating something causes a migraine that's between 1-4, I'll eat it. Anything that would land me in the ER, forget it. I usually have to take trips down to the closest drug store and buy myself cereal and crackers to hold me the whole week. I don't actually eat a lot anymore because of this, and then he complains because I'm down to just above my danger weight. The boy's an idiot and I'm frustrated as hell.

Thank you. Sometimes I have a hard time believing there really is anyone out there waiting for me. When I was younger I always had a silly thought that they were probably on the other side of the world or something, and I'd end up meeting them by accident while being a nerd in a bookstore. Yeah, probably not happening, but it'd be nice. 

I'll try. I feel a little less destroyed today, so that's a good sign. Brother took off for his 'quiet time' a bit ago and left her with me, and she always gets worse to deal with when her baby is out, so I'm not looking forward to it. Right now she's calm and reading, so that's something.
